claim: Given a .docx package and a target string that occurs exactly once (counting overlapping occurrences) in the visible text of the paragraphs of word/document.xml - possibly spanning several runs and text nodes - produce a package whose paragraph texts equal the originals with that single span replaced, with the same number of paragraphs and text nodes and every other member byte-identical; when the target occurs zero or several times, fail closed and write nothing.
input_class: Structurally real WordprocessingML packages (content types, package/document rels, styles, core properties, optional binary media), 1-12 paragraphs, 1-5 runs each, random run properties, xml:space=preserve, Unicode and XML-special characters, numbered tokens; target cut from the paragraph text (at least 8 characters where the text allows, 70 % across a run boundary) in 68 % of instances, absent in 12 %, planted 1-2 more times in 13 %, self-overlapping periodic target (u*2 inside u*3) in 7 %; short or repeated cuts make further instances non-unique by chance; replacement may be empty, equal (no-op) or longer than the target. Measured mix on a 2000-instance dry run: PASS 65 %, fail-closed non-unique 35 %.
scope_limits: NO visual-layout, tracked-changes, fields or numbering guarantees
NO general DOCX editing; one span per call

solver.note: the kernel is byte-pinned by a governance record, so the pure adapter lives in a separate module; the receipt records the kernel blob too

declared.lineage: derived from the claim; minidom paragraph-text model with overlapping occurrence count, never ElementTree

falsification_condition: Any generated package on which a unique span is not replaced exactly as the paragraph-text model predicts with all other members byte-identical, or on which an absent or repeated target does not fail closed without output.
history: Component of the ARTIFACT_CREATION family route (Brain-owned DOCX skills); kernel byte-pinned by a governance record and never measured on fresh instances before 2026-10-14. Measured through canonical/runtime/docx_true_capability_adapters_v1.py (pure base64/tempfile adapter) so the pinned kernel stays untouched; the receipt records the kernel blob. Measured 2026-10-14: 2000/2000 on first run, no defect found; ten scratch mutants all caught by the oracles.
